question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class configurable filesystem allow/deny policy, and should the first accepted scope include arbitrary shell `exec` access or split exec into a separate tracked boundary?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent config shape, default behavior, migration story, and exec coverage define an operator-facing security boundary that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Land file policy with explicit exec split
options.body: Define `tools.fs.allowedPaths` and `tools.fs.denyPaths` for file tools, apply_patch, and local media while documenting and tracking exec as a separate policy boundary.

options.title: Design one file-plus-exec RWX policy
options.body: Treat this issue and the path-scoped exec/RWX discussion as one larger product surface, accepting a broader implementation and proof cost.

options.title: Reject native path ACLs for now
options.body: Close the native config request and document Docker, OS user isolation, and plugin hooks as the supported mitigation path.

recommendation.title: Land file policy with explicit exec split
recommendation.body: Define `tools.fs.allowedPaths` and `tools.fs.denyPaths` for file tools, apply_patch, and local media while documenting and tracking exec as a separate policy boundary.
